title: Report a current judge fail ahead of an unverifiable one on the same step
body:
## Summary
When a step holds both an unknown-provenance and a current judge fail, the acceptance path and /status report whichever comes first.

## Description
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/judgeBridge.ts:158 and src/lib/status/statusModel.ts:598 both take the first condemning fail from `classified`. The status is right either way, but the attribution and reason can say VERDICT: UNVERIFIED with an `[unverified provenance]` caveat while a confirmed current fail exists. Fixed means both sites prefer `current`, then `unknown`, through one shared picker.

## Flow
- Add a shared picker beside CONDEMNING_PROVENANCE in judgeBridge.ts
- Use it in bridgeJudgeVerdict and deriveCell
- Test order [unknown human, current vlm] on both surfaces

## Expected impact
An operator sees the strongest evidence and does not re-judge a step that already holds a confirmed fail. Only attribution and reason text change, never the status.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the reported condemnation is the best-bound one
Before: by reading, [unknown, current] attributes the unknown verdict at both sites
After: predicted current verdict attributed at both sites
Method: simulation - statusModel.ts is outside this context, so one half could not be built here
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/lib/catalog/acceptance/judgeBridge.ts:158 classified.find((c) => CONDEMNS.has(c.p)); src/lib/status/statusModel.ts:598 classified.find((c) => c.v.verdict === 'fail' && CONDEMNING_PROVENANCE.has(c.p))
instrument: A test feeding [unknown, current] fails to bridgeJudgeVerdict and deriveCell, asserting the current verdict is attributed by both

title: Single-source the judge provenance notes written in two files
body:
## Summary
The provenance sentences shown for a judge verdict are written separately in judgeBridge.ts and statusModel.ts.

## Description
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/judgeBridge.ts:170-184 and src/lib/status/statusModel.ts:507-523 (`provenanceNote`) carry the same four sentences: current, unverified-but-applied, stale, superseded. A wording change to one leaves the lab and /status disagreeing. statusModel already imports from judgeBridge, so the function can move there without a cycle. The judgeBridge-only line for a checker that had already not passed stays local.

## Flow
- Move provenanceNote into judgeBridge.ts and export it
- Call it from attribute sites in bridgeJudgeVerdict
- Import it in statusModel.ts
- Pin that both surfaces emit the same note for each provenance

## Expected impact
Developers change this copy in one place, and the two surfaces cannot drift. Risk is limited to tests that pin the exact sentences.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source for the provenance copy
Before: 4 sentences written at 2 sites
After: predicted 4 sentences at 1 site
Method: simulation - the change requires statusModel.ts, outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Count duplicated sentence literals across the two files, plus a parity test over all four provenances

title: Decide whether a python drain bridge error should stop its chain
body:
## Summary
A bridge error on one python step leaves the chain running, so later steps can run after an upstream step that never ran.

## Description
src/lib/catalog/acceptance/pythonDrain.ts:152-156 records `bridge-error` and continues without setting `broken`. If the bridge recovers mid-chain, the next module runs without its predecessor, and a failure it returns is saved as a real `fail`. The file header calls that kind of consequence noise, but its stop rule names only condemned steps, and it also says could-not-ask is not a failure. Fixed means a transport error stops the chain with a distinct outcome that writes nothing.

## Flow
- Step 1 returns bridge-error
- The bridge recovers
- Step 2 runs without step 1 and returns failed items
- Step 2 is saved as fail

## Expected impact
A transient editor hiccup no longer records false downstream failures. Could break a caller that relies on later independent steps still running after a transport error.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no recorded cascade from a step that never ran
Before: by reading, a chain [error, ok-run] dispatches step 2 and saves its verdict
After: predicted step 2 is not dispatched and nothing is saved
Method: simulation - whether the modules are independent needs checking against the UE project's player_movement scripts, which this round did not read
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: A pythonDrain test with run returning an error then a failed return, plus a read of the player_movement module dependencies

title: Stop the coach summary saying waiting on Unreal for generator deferrals
body:
## Summary
The entity summary describes every deferred step as waiting on Unreal, including gallery steps that are waiting on a generator run.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/labGlossary.ts `plainEntitySummary` writes `still waiting on a live Unreal test` and `N waiting on Unreal` from one `deferred` count. src/lib/catalog/rollup.ts counts all L3 and L4 deferrals together, and galleryArtifact.ts defers swatch selections at L4 with the reason `Run the generator`. There are 47 `selected(` gallery checkers in src/lib/catalog/pipelines. Fixed means the rollup separates waiting-on-generator from waiting-on-Unreal, or the copy stops naming the cause.

## Flow
- Produce a gallery step in stub mode
- It defers at L4 because the selection is a swatch
- NextStepCoach renders plainEntitySummary
- The summary says the step waits on a live Unreal test

## Expected impact
Artists are told the real next act, generate art, rather than to wait for an Unreal run. A split changes the EntityRollup shape, which several surfaces read.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the summary names the true blocker
Before: 47 gallery checkers can defer into a sentence that names Unreal
After: predicted 0 generator deferrals described as Unreal
Method: simulation - the honest split needs rollup.ts, outside this context, and a way to tell the cause from a row
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: A rollup test over mixed gallery-swatch and L3 deferrals asserting the summary names each cause correctly
